title: Rotatory Antenna System
tagline: A rotating antenna station that tracks LEO satellites across the sky in real time and captures their signals — built end to end, from hardware to web interface.
summary: End to end: 3D-modelled hardware, part selection, motor firmware, C code that reads TLE data and propagates orbits with SGP4, and a PHP web interface to control it all.
overview: I designed and built a modular rotating structure that points highly directive antennas at satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO) and follows them across the sky in real time.

Until then, the team captured signals with directive antennas pointed straight up at the zenith, which limited how much of each satellite pass they could record. A tracking antenna stays on target for the whole pass, expanding the team's signal-capture capabilities.

The work covered every layer of the system: the mechanical design and parts, the firmware that drives the motors, the C code that predicts where each satellite will be, and the web interface researchers use to control it.
The project was also my bachelor's thesis for the Telecommunications Electronics Engineering degree at UAB.
